    Corporate Profile
    Aluminum Corporation of China Limited (“Chalco” or the “Company”) is a joint stock limited
    company established in the People’s Republic of China (the “PRC”); its shares are listed on The
    Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (the “Hong Kong Stock Exchange”) and the Shanghai
    Stock Exchange (“SSE”), respectively.


    The Company and its subsidiaries (the “Group”) is a leading enterprise in aluminum industry in
    China, ranking among the top in the global aluminum industry in terms of overall strengths. The
    Group’s alumina, fine alumina, electrolytic aluminum, high purity aluminum and gallium metal
    production capacity all rank first in the world, and is a large manufacturer and operator with
    integration of exploration and mining of bauxite, coal and other resources; production, sales and
    technology research of alumina, primary aluminum, aluminum alloy and carbon; international trade;
    logistics business; thermal and new energy power generation.


    The core competitiveness of the Group is mainly reflected in:


    •     its clear and stable development, strategy facilitating steady progress towards high-quality
          growth;


    •     its synergistic and efficient industrial layout, creating a prominent competitive edge across
          the entire industry chain;


    •     its strong technological innovation capabilities, continuously leading the advancement of the
          industry;


    •     its exceptional brand image, demonstrating an increasingly evident brand value advantage;


    •     its excellent management team and operational mechanism, ensuring the stable development
          of the Company.


    As at the end of the Reporting Period, the Group is principally comprised of the following branches,
    subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates:


    Major Branches:


    •     Guangxi branch (mainly engaged in the production and sale of alumina products);


    •     Qinghai branch (mainly engaged in the production and sale of primary aluminum and alloy
          products);


    •     Guizhou branch (mainly engaged in bauxite mining, production and sale of alloy products);


    •     Liancheng branch (mainly engaged in the production and sale of primary aluminum products);

2.   DIRECTORS AND SENIOR MANAGEMENT AS AT THE
     DATE OF THIS ANNUAL REPORT

     Major Working Experience of Directors and Senior Management of the Company as at the
     Date of this Annual Report:


     Executive Directors

     Mr. He Wenjian, aged 57, is the chairman, an Executive Director and the secretary of
     the Party committee of the Company. Mr. He graduated from Central South University of
     Technology majoring in industrial management engineering, holds a bachelor’s degree in
     engineering and is a senior engineer with extensive experience in corporate management
     and production technology. Mr. He successively served as the deputy manager and manager
     of the planning management department of Qinghai branch of the Company, an assistant
     to the general manager and the head of the aluminum carbon plant of Qinghai branch, the
     senior manager and deputy general manager of the corporate management department of the
     Company, while concurrently serving as a director of Shanxi Huaze Aluminum & Power Co.,
     Ltd.* (山西華澤鋁電有限公司) and a director of Zunyi Aluminum (遵義鋁業), the deputy director
     of the corporate management department of Aluminum Corporation of China* (中國鋁業公
     司), the general manager and secretary of the Party committee of Liancheng branch of the
     Company, the chairman of the board of directors of Lanzhou Liancheng Aluminum Co., Ltd.*
     (蘭州連城鋁業有限責任公司), the general manager of the operation optimization department
     (reform office) of Chinalco, while concurrently serving as a director of Gansu Hualu (甘肅華鷺),
     a supervisor of China Aluminum International Engineering Corporation Limited (中鋁國際工程

4.   DECISION MAKING PROCESS AND BASIS OF
     DETERMINATION OF REMUNERATION OF DIRECTORS
     AND SENIOR MANAGEMENT AND REMUNERATION

     The human resources department of the Company formulates the annual remuneration
     proposals for the Directors (limited to those who receive remuneration from the Company,
     the same below) and senior management in accordance with the Company’s remuneration
     policy and with reference to market standards. These proposals will be submitted to
     the Board of Directors of the Company for consideration after being approved by the
     Remuneration Committee of the Board of Directors of the Company. Specifically, the
     remuneration proposal for senior management will be reviewed and approved by the Board of
     Directors of the Company, while the remuneration proposals for Directors will be submitted
     to the shareholders’ general meeting for consideration and approval after being approved by
     the Board of Directors of the Company.


     The Remuneration Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors has reviewed and
     approved the annual remuneration standards for the Company’s Directors and senior
     management, as well as the annual performance responsibility agreements for senior
     management. The Remuneration Committee considers that the remuneration standards
     formulated by the Company align with the Company’s remuneration policy and have been
     benchmarked against the compensation levels of comparable positions within the industry
     in which the Company operates and enterprises of similar scale. Additionally, the annual
     performance responsibility agreements for senior management are consistent with the
     Company’s actual production and operations, featuring comprehensive indicators and
     reasonable weightings, which can effectively constrain and motivate the management to fulfill
     their duties with diligence. Therefore, the committee agrees to submit these remuneration
     matters to the Company’s Board of Directors for consideration.


     The Company determines and implements the remuneration for its Directors and senior
     management based on its established remuneration policy, taking into account its annual
     operating results, the fulfillment of duties by the Directors, and the appraisal results for
     performance of senior management.




                                                                               2025 ANNUAL REPORT    25
     Directors, Senior Management and Employees (Continued)

          The Company has implemented an annual salary system for its senior management. The
          remuneration structure comprises basic remuneration, performance-based remuneration,
          bonuses for exceeding targets, tenure incentives, special awards, and allowances and
          subsidies. Among these: basic remuneration is the annual basic income received by senior
          management for performing their normal duties and is paid monthly based on their positions;
          performance-based remuneration and bonuses for exceeding targets are paid based on
          the results of the annual performance appraisal and are generally deferred over a three-
          year period; tenure incentives are paid based on the results of the tenure performance
          appraisal and are generally paid after the end of the tenure; special awards are granted to
          senior management for making outstanding contributions to special key initiatives such as
          the Company’s reform and development, transformation and upgrading, cost reduction and
          efficiency enhancement, and scientific and technological innovation, and are paid immediately
          upon meeting the award conditions; allowances and subsidies are paid according to the
          cycles stipulated in the Company’s relevant policies.


          The Company continues to improve the incentive and restraint mechanism linking the
          remuneration of senior management to performance appraisals, adhering to a remuneration
          management system based on position value and performance contribution. The fixed portion
          of remuneration is determined based on position, while the proportion of the variable portion is
          further increased and strongly linked to appraisal results to create a reasonable gap in income
          distribution.


          In 2025, the total pre-tax remunerations of the Directors and senior management received
          from the Company amounted to RMB11.36 million (including the remuneration of the
          Independent Non-executive Directors).

The Company has been committed to the principle of employment equality between men
and women and prohibited gender-based discrimination. However, as the Company is mainly
engaged in the smelting and manufacturing of non-ferrous metals, many production posts in
the Company are labour intensive and are not suitable for female employees due to objective
factors such as physical fitness and working environment. In order to protect women’s
employment rights, the Company arranges as many jobs as possible for female employees.
As of the end of the Reporting Period, the proportion of female employees in the total staff of
the Company was 14.60%.

As of the end of the Reporting Period, there was one female member of the Board and the
senior management added one female member in 2025. The Company will adhere to the
principle of gender diversity at all employee levels and will appropriately consider increasing
the proportion of female members in future elections, hirings and promotions.

     2.   APPROVAL OF SHARE CHANGES AND SHARE TRANSFERS

          (1) Repurchase and Cancellation of Restricted Shares
                On 19 November 2024, the Company convened the 28th meeting of the eighth session
                of the Board and the 15th meeting of the eighth session of the Supervisory Committee,
                at which the Resolution on Repurchase and Cancellation of Partial Restricted Shares
                Granted to Participants but Not Yet Unlocked and Adjustment to the Repurchase Price
                was considered and approved, and it was agreed that the Company would repurchase
                and cancel the 866,831 restricted shares which had been granted to 36 Incentive
                Participants but not yet unlocked at the adjusted repurchase price of RMB2.85 per
                share (first grant) and RMB2.01 per share (reserved grant). The Company had paid the
                full amount for repurchase of the restricted shares of RMB2,329,008.08 to the aforesaid
                36 Incentive Participants.

                On 27 January 2025, the Company received the Certificate of Change in Registration
                of Securities issued by CSDC Shanghai Branch, confirming that the procedures for the
                repurchase and cancellation of 866,831 Restricted Shares as mentioned above were
                completed on 24 January 2025. Accordingly, the total share capital of the Company
                changed from 17,156,498,909 shares to 17,155,632,078 shares.

                For details of the above, please refer to the relevant announcements of the Company
                dated 19 November 2024, 21 January 2025 and 27 January 2025, respectively.

                On 24 November and 25 November 2025, the Company convened the 1st meeting of
                the Remuneration Committee of the ninth session of the Board and the 7th meeting of
                the ninth session of the Board, at which the Resolution on Repurchase and Cancellation
                of Partial Restricted Shares Granted to Participants but Not Yet Unlocked and
                Adjustment to the Repurchase Price was considered and approved, and it was agreed
                that the Company would repurchase and cancel the 660,751 restricted shares which
                had been granted to 15 Incentive Participants but not yet unlocked at the adjusted
                repurchase price of RMB2.60 per share (first grant) and RMB1.76 per share (reserved
                grant). The Company had paid the full amount for repurchase of the restricted shares of
                RMB1,724,055.20 to the aforesaid 15 Incentive Participants.

                On 4 February 2026, the Company received the Certificate of Change in Registration
                of Securities issued by CSDC Shanghai Branch, confirming that the procedures for the
                repurchase and cancellation of 660,751 Restricted Shares as mentioned above were
                completed on 3 February 2026. Accordingly, the total share capital of the Company
                changed from 17,155,632,078 shares to 17,154,971,327 shares.

                For details of the above, please refer to the relevant announcements of the Company
                dated 25 November 2025, 30 January 2026 and 4 February 2026, respectively.

     (2) Unlocking and Listing of Restricted Shares

          On 28 May 2025, the 34th meeting of the eighth session of the Board and the 18th
          meeting of the eighth session of the Supervisory Committee of the Company were
          held, respectively, at which the Resolution on Satisfaction of the Unlocking Conditions
          for the Second Unlocking Period of the Restricted Shares Under the First Grant of
          the 2021 Restricted Share Incentive Scheme was considered and passed, and it was
          agreed that the Company would deal with the unlocking procedures for the 32,083,238
          Restricted Shares which satisfy the unlocking conditions for the second Unlocking
          Period under the first grant. Subsequently, with the approval of CSDC Shanghai Branch
          and SSE, the aforesaid Restricted Shares which satisfy the unlocking conditions were
          formally tradable on 13 June 2025.


          For details of the above, please refer to the relevant announcements of the Company
          dated 28 May 2025 and 6 June 2025, respectively.


          On 24 November and 25 November 2025, the 1st meeting of the Remuneration
          Committee of the ninth session of the Board and the 7th meeting of the ninth session
          of the Board of the Company were held, respectively, at which the Resolution on
          Satisfaction of the Unlocking Conditions for the Second Unlocking Period of the
          Restricted Shares Under the Reserved Grant of the 2021 Restricted Share Incentive
          Scheme was considered and passed, and it was agreed that the Company would
          deal with the unlocking procedures for the 7,742,752 Restricted Shares which satisfy
          the unlocking conditions for the second Unlocking Period under the reserved grant.
          Subsequently, with the approval of CSDC Shanghai Branch and SSE, the aforesaid
          Restricted Shares which satisfy the unlocking conditions were formally tradable on 23
          December 2025.


          For details of the above, please refer to the relevant announcements of the Company
          dated 25 November 2025 and 15 December 2025, respectively.


          The unlocking and listing of the aforementioned restricted shares will only affect the
          quantity of the Company’s shares subject to trading restrictions and shares not subject
          to trading restrictions, and will not result in any changes to the total share capital of the
          Company.

MARKET REVIEW OF THE ALUMINUM INDUSTRY CHAIN

Bauxite: The global diversification of bauxite resource allocation is
gathering pace, with supply chain security steadily consolidated.

In 2025, China’s domestic bauxite market saw prominent supply rigidity amid ongoing environmental
and safety supervision, changes in ore grade and other factors, while overall market performance
remained relatively stable. In contrast, the overseas market presented a loose supply pattern. With
the release of production capacity in major producing regions such as Guinea, global bauxite supply
recorded a notable increase. Although import ore prices saw a phased rebound in the second
quarter due to short-term policy disturbances, the annual price center of imported bauxite trended
downwards against the backdrop of overall ample global supply.


In 2025, China’s bauxite imports continued to rise, with cumulative imports for the year reaching
200 million tonnes, representing a year-on-year increase of 26.3%. Key sources of imports included
Guinea, Australia, Turkey, Sierra Leone, Guyana, Malaysia and other countries, demonstrating
the diversified resource allocation capabilities of China’s aluminum industry. Of this total, imports
of bauxite from Guinea amounted to 150 million tonnes, representing a year-on-year increase
of 35.2%, accounting for 74.3% of total imports; imports of bauxite from Australia amounted to
37.35 million tonnes, representing a year-on-year decrease of 6.4%, accounting for 18.6% of total
imports. Domestic bauxite production for the year reached 73 million tonnes, roughly flat compared
to the previous year.




                                                                                  2025 ANNUAL REPORT    43
     Chairman’s Statement (Continued)

     Alumina: The pattern of tight market supply has eased somewhat,
     with the price level trending lower gradually.

     In 2025, against the backdrop of relatively loose overall supply in China’s domestic alumina
     industry, prices trended downwards overall. In the first half of the year, as new production
     capacity in Shandong, Hebei and other regions was successively commissioned and entered a
     stable operation phase, market supply increased, driving a substantial decline in alumina prices.
     In response to changes in the operating environment following the price adjustment, large-scale
     maintenance shutdowns and flexible production were implemented across the industry, which
     eased the supply-demand pattern somewhat and led to a phased rebound in prices. In the second
     half of the year, as previously idled capacity from maintenance resumed operation and new
     projects ramped up production, market supply pressure re-emerged, and alumina prices re-entered
     a downward trajectory. In 2025, the average domestic spot price of alumina was RMB3,221 per
     tonne, representing a year-on-year decrease of 21.1%. In the international market, the overall trend
     of alumina prices was basically consistent with that of the domestic market, with a full-year average
     price of USD388 per tonne, representing a year-on-year decrease of 22.7%.


     In terms of supply and demand, the domestic alumina market overall presented a pattern of supply
     exceeding demand in 2025. New production capacity for the year reached 10.3 million tonnes, with
     output increasing by 8.3% year-on-year. On the demand side, electrolytic aluminum production
     capacity increasingly approached its “ceiling”, with output growth slowing down, driving the
     alumina market to shift from a tight balance to oversupply. Meanwhile, China’s alumina market
     registered a net export pattern in 2025, which alleviated domestic supply pressure to a certain
     extent. For the full year, cumulative alumina exports reached 2.55 million tonnes, up 42.5% year-
     on-year, with net exports amounting to 1.35 million tonnes, representing a year-on-year increase of
     264.9%.


     According to the statistics, the global output and consumption of alumina for 2025 were 150.49
     million tonnes and 147.33 million tonnes, respectively, representing a year-on-year increase of
     6.0% and 1.9%, respectively; the domestic output and consumption of alumina were approximately
     92.94 million tonnes and 88.67 million tonnes, respectively, representing a year-on-year increase of
     8.3% and 1.9%, respectively, accounting for 61.8% and 60.2% of global output and consumption,
     respectively. As of the end of December 2025, the alumina capacity utilization rate in the world was
     75.6%, while that of the PRC was 80.9%.




44   ALUMINUM CORPORATION OF CHINA LIMITED
                                                         Chairman’s Statement (Continued)

Primary Aluminum: The robust supply-demand structure, coupled
with the support from its financial and strategic attributes,
provides solid underpinning, with the price level trending higher
continuously.

In 2025, the trading range for domestic and international aluminum prices shifted upwards,
with prices remaining at high levels. From the beginning of the year to mid-March, aluminum
prices showed a relatively strong trend, influenced by factors such as declining inventories and a
weakening U.S. dollar. From mid-March to early April, as the China-U.S. trade war escalated and
the plummeting price of alumina removed cost support for electrolytic aluminum, aluminum prices
underwent a deep correction, falling to the lowest point of the year. From mid-April to year-end,
benefiting from multiple positive factors such as the easing of China-U.S. economic and trade
relations, overseas primary aluminum supply disruptions, support from the upward-shifting cost
center, and the Federal Reserve’s interest rate cuts, domestic and overseas aluminum prices
trended steadily higher, reaching a yearly high at the end of the year and setting a new high for
the past three years. In 2025, the average prices of aluminum on the SHFE for the spot-month
contract and the three-month futures contract were RMB20,750 per tonne and 20,698 per tonne,
representing year-on-year increases of 4.0% and 3.5%, respectively. On the LME, the average
prices for spot-month contract and the three-month futures contract stood at USD2,632 per tonne
and USD2,641 per tonne, representing year-on-year increases of 8.8% and 7.5%, respectively.




                                                                               2025 ANNUAL REPORT    45
     Chairman’s Statement (Continued)

     In terms of supply and demand, China’s electrolytic aluminum production capacity saw stable
     growth in 2025, with a slight increase in output, marking the lowest growth rate since 2020. The
     scale of production resumption for the year was 550,000 tonnes per annum, and new production
     capacity was 180,000 tonnes per annum. As of the end of 2025, domestic operating capacity of
     electrolytic aluminum reached 44.83 million tonnes per annum, basically hitting the “ceiling”, with
     an increase of only 270,000 tonnes from the previous year. On the demand side, while the real
     estate remained sluggish, sectors such as home appliances, new energy vehicles, power, and 3C
     electronics maintained strong growth, supporting the continued expansion of the consumer market.
     Considering the production, sales, and import volumes for the full year, the supply and demand for
     electrolytic aluminum were in a tight balance.


     According to the statistics, the global output and consumption of primary aluminum for 2025 were
     74.52 million tonnes and 74.53 million tonnes, respectively, representing a year-on-year increase
     of 1.9% and 2.2%, respectively; the domestic output and consumption of primary aluminum were
     44.23 million tonnes and 46.29 million tonnes, respectively, representing a year-on-year increase of
     1.8% and 2.5%, respectively, accounting for 59.4% and 62.1% of global output and consumption,
     respectively. Amid the exit of inefficient capacity and slow growth in total capacity, high profits
     in the aluminum industry in recent years have driven the production enthusiasm of electrolytic
     aluminum enterprises, with the entire industry maintaining a high operating rate. As of the end
     of 2025, the capacity utilization rate of primary aluminum in the world was 93.5%, while that of
     primary aluminum in the PRC was 98.5%.

BUSINESS REVIEW

In 2025, amid complex and evolving external circumstances, the Company firmly seized strategic
initiative, proactively responded to the volatile external environment, intensified strategic operation,
focused on cost reduction and efficiency enhancement, accelerated structural adjustment, and
deepened reform and innovation. It successfully accomplished annual production and operation
targets as well as reform and development objectives, achieving a high-quality conclusion to the
14th Five-Year Plan period.


1.    New Leap in Value Creation
      The Company strengthened overall budget guidance, achieved efficient collaboration across
      production, supply, transportation, marketing, R&D and finance, significantly enhanced rapid
      monetization capacity, and steadily improved the quality of production and operation. Major
      products maintained stable and high output, and the internal supporting ratio of ore, alumina
      and primary aluminum was further optimized. The Company continued to deepen full-factor
      benchmarking, with major energy consumption indicators such as comprehensive AC power
      consumption per ton of primary aluminum and comprehensive energy consumption per ton of
      alumina continuing to decline, further strengthening cost competitiveness. For the full year,
      the Company achieved a total profit of RMB25.840 billion, a net profit of RMB21.525 billion
      and operating net cash flow of RMB33.843 billion, reaching a record high.


2.    New Pattern in Structural Optimization

      In line with the Company’s strategic development plan, the Company continuously enhanced
      bauxite resource acquisition capacity, further consolidating the foundation for resource
      security. It accelerated the optimization of industrial layout and structural adjustment,
      systematically implemented the overseas development strategy, and continuously improved
      the Company’s resource allocation and integration capabilities in the global industrial
      chain. Alumina production capacity was steadily clustered in coastal areas with advantages
      in resources, energy and logistics. Primary aluminum production adhered to the green
      transformation of energy structure and was orderly optimized to regions with clean energy
      advantages. A number of energy-saving renovation, recycled aluminum and high-tech projects

2026 marks the first year of the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Against the dual background of global

      Competitiveness

      supporting capacity of bauxite, alumina and primary aluminum, optimize the product mix
      of fine alumina, aluminum alloys, gallium metal and other products, enhance product
      competitiveness and profitability.


2.    Deepen Global Layout to Enhance Industrial Chain Resilience

      The Company will focus on the layout and operational coordination of domestic and overseas
      projects, actively promote overseas bauxite resource acquisition and the implementation of
      strategic projects. Leveraging its full industrial chain advantages, management advantages

      chain system to enhance international competitive resilience and risk resistance.


3.    Strengthen Green Drivers to Enhance Sustainable
      Development Leadership

      structure, increasing the proportion of new energy usage, promoting the application of

      the green value of products. The Company will vigorously develop circular economy such
      as recycled aluminum and red mud comprehensive utilization, strengthen the integrated
      development of “source-grid-load-storage”, and forge new competitive advantages in green
      and low-carbon development.

BUSINESS SEGMENTS
The Group principally engages in the exploration and mining of bauxite, coal and other resources;
the production, sales and technical development of alumina, primary aluminum, aluminum alloy and
carbon products; international trading, logistics services, as well as electricity generation from coal
and new energy. The main business segments of the Group comprise:

Alumina segment mainly consists of mining and purchasing bauxite and other raw materials, refining
bauxite into alumina, and selling alumina both internally to the Group’s electrolytic aluminum
enterprises and marketing enterprises and externally to customers outside the Group. This segment
also includes the production and sales of refined alumina and gallium.

Primary aluminum segment mainly consists of procuring alumina, raw and auxiliary materials and
electricity power, smelting alumina to produce primary aluminum, and selling them internally to
the Group’s trading enterprises and externally to customers outside the Group. This segment also
includes the production and sales of carbon products, aluminum alloy products and other electrolytic
aluminum products.

Marketing segment is mainly engaged in the marketing and logistics of alumina, primary aluminum,
other nonferrous metal products, and crude fuels such as coal products, as well as raw and auxiliary
materials to internal enterprises of the Group and external customers.

Energy segment mainly consists of coal, electricity generation from coal, wind power and
photovoltaic power and new energy equipment production, etc. Among its major products, coals are
sold to internal enterprises of the Group and external customers outside the Group; and electricity
power generated by public power plants, wind power and photovoltaic power stations of the Group is
sold to local grid companies.

Corporate and other operating segments include the headquarter of the Company and research and
development and other activities of other aluminum-related business.


OPERATING RESULT
For the year ended 31 December 2025, the Group’s net profit attributable to shareholders of the
Company amounted to RMB12,674 million, representing an increase of RMB279 million or 2.25%
from RMB12,395 million in the prior year. Such growth was primarily attributable to the Group’s
adherence to the philosophy of operational excellence throughout the year. Through strengthened
operational management and control, enhanced extreme cost reduction, and establishing a safe,
efficient, and low-cost supply chain system, as well as seizing market opportunities, the Group
effectively lifted its capacity utilisation rate, with its operating results hitting a record high for the
history.

PROVISION FOR INVENTORY IMPAIRMENT

As at 31 December 2025, the Group assessed the net realisable value ("NRV”) of its inventories on
an individual basis. For inventories related to aluminum products, the Group assessed the NRV of
inventories based on the estimated selling price of finished products when available for sale, with
reference to the production and sales linkage scheme between the Group’s alumina enterprises and
electrolytic aluminum enterprises, combined with relevant financial budgets, and taking into account
factors including the inventory turnover period, the purpose of the Group’s inventory holdings, and
the impact of events after the balance sheet date. For inventories held by the Energy Segment, the
NRV was uniformly derived from the latest market prices.


As at 31 December 2025, the balance of provision for inventory impairment of the Group’s
inventories amounted to RMB399 million, representing a decrease of RMB37 million from RMB436
million as at the end of 2024.


The Company has always adopted the same approach to determine the NRV of its inventories and
the provision for inventory impairment on a consistent basis for the relevant accounting policy.

     PRINCIPAL ACTIVITIES

     The Company is a leading enterprise in aluminum industry in China, and ranks among the top
     enterprises in global aluminum industry in terms of comprehensive strength. The Company’s
     alumina, fine alumina, electrolytic aluminum, high-purity aluminum and gallium metal production
     capacity all rank first in the world. The Company’s main business includes exploration and mining
     of resources such as bauxite and coal, production, sales, technology research and development
     of alumina, primary aluminum, aluminum alloys, and carbon products, international trade, logistics
     industry, thermal and new energy power generation, etc.


     BUSINESS MODEL

     Based on the domestic circulation and international circulation, the Company takes value creation as
     its guiding principle to improve and strengthen five traditional industries, namely mineral resources,
     alumina, electrolytic aluminum, carbon and power generation; to refine and specialize in six new
     industries, namely, fine alumina, aluminum alloy, high-purity aluminum, new energy, small metals
     and comprehensive utilization of resources; and to make the three platform industries of trade,
     logistics and materials more practical and better, thereby building a “5-6-3” industrial development
     pattern to become an outstanding main force in technological innovation, a ballast stone in mineral
     resources, a pillar in high-end advanced materials, and a leader in green, low-carbon, and low-cost
     digital intelligence with the goal of building a world-class mining and aluminum company with global
     competitiveness. Pursuing openness and cooperation, the Company builds an integrated supply
     chain platform based on three major platforms to integrate production, trading, finance, storage,
     transportation, information and information, etc. The Company is constantly fostering and improving
     a business model that focuses on product value creation and is closely integrated with value added
     financial trade. Through the optimal allocation of the value chain, enterprise chain, supply and
     demand chain and spatial chain, the Company has created a win-win situation featuring synergy and
     efficiency, as well as cost reduction between the upper-, middle-and lower-streams of the industrial
     chain for the Company and its affiliated enterprises.

     INDUSTRY LANDSCAPE AND TRENDS

     Policy empowerment and green transition drive a new pattern of high-quality development.
     The aluminum industry is a fundamental industry supporting national economic development
     and strategic security, with an industrial chain covering the entire process from bauxite mining,
     alumina smelting to primary aluminum production and intensive processing. As one of the most
     widely used and consumed non-ferrous metals in the global industrial system, aluminum is not
     only a basic raw material for traditional sectors such as transportation, construction, power and
     machinery manufacturing, but also an indispensable key supporting material for aerospace, high-end
     equipment and high-tech industries. Thanks to its green properties of light weight, high strength,
     corrosion resistance, good electrical conductivity and recyclability, aluminum plays an increasingly
     important role in the new round of energy transformation and industrial upgrading. Currently,
     with the construction of the global green economic system, the application of aluminum alloys in
     emerging sectors such as automotive lightweighting, photovoltaic modules, charging piles, energy
     storage equipment and consumer electronics continues to expand, making the aluminum industry
     more closely linked to the macroeconomy, energy structure and environmental protection policies.


     Targeted policy support injects new impetus into industrial development. In 2025, driven by
     both policies and the market, China’s aluminum industry accelerated high-quality development.
     A series of policy documents including the Aluminum Industry High-quality Development
     Implementation Plan (2025–2027) (《鋁產業高質量發展實施方案(2025–2027年)》)and the Notice
     on Matters Concerning the Orderly Promotion of Direct Green Power Connection (《關於有序推
     動綠電直連發展有關事項的通知》)were successively issued, systematically guiding the industry to
     upgrade toward high-end, intelligent and green development. The industrial structure continued
     to optimize, with an obvious trend of high-end and green transformation. Alumina and primary
     aluminum output grew steadily, and the supply capacity of high-end aluminum processed products
     improved significantly. Remarkable results were achieved in green and low-carbon transformation,
     with the proportion of green power aluminum rising to 27.7% and recycled aluminum accounting
     for 20.8%, helping the industry achieve carbon peaking six years ahead of schedule. Significant
     progress was made in technological breakthroughs, with digital intelligence empowering
     industrial upgrading. Core technologies and equipment reached international advanced levels,
     and AI technology was applied on a large scale in scenarios such as production control and fault
     resolution. Emerging consumption sectors rose, reshaping the market demand pattern. New
     energy vehicles, photovoltaics, power grids and other emerging sectors became new engines
     for aluminum consumption growth, driving overall demand growth. China’s aluminum output
     and consumption have ranked first in the world for 24 consecutive years, accounting for 35% of
     China’s total non-ferrous metal output value, further consolidating its pillar position. The supply
     and demand structure remained stable, and aluminum prices fluctuated cyclically. In 2025,
     the global economy showed certain resilience amid complex and volatile conditions, monetary
     policies of major economies shifted to easing, domestic primary aluminum supply growth stabilized,
     overseas supply disturbances intensified, and global primary aluminum capacity utilization remained




64   ALUMINUM CORPORATION OF CHINA LIMITED
                                                               Report of the Board (Continued)

high. Affected by multiple factors such as macroeconomy, geopolitics, supply and demand pattern
and technological progress, aluminum prices fluctuated cyclically. The industry is in a critical period
of green transition, structural optimization and capacity upgrading, with policy orientation, resource
endowment and technological innovation dominating the industry landscape.


Looking ahead to 2026, the global bauxite market is expected to maintain a loose supply pattern,
but attention should be paid to disturbances caused by uncertainties in mining policies of major
resource countries. Barring major supply disruptions, imported ore prices may fluctuate weakly.
In the alumina market, new domestic alumina capacity and overseas projects will continue to be
commissioned, and the overcapacity situation is difficult to reverse in the short term. Despite
supply pressure, the industry will enter a period of in-depth structural adjustment, with high-cost,
high-energy consumption and technologically backward capacity likely to be phased out at an
accelerated pace. The market is expected to develop toward higher quality in the game of supply
and demand rebalancing. In the primary aluminum market will see exacerbated primary aluminum
price fluctuations due to external factors. Domestic supply will remain stable, slow overseas
commissioning and potential production reduction risks will limit global supply growth, while
demand in transportation, electronic power, low-altitude economy and other sectors is expected to
maintain a good momentum. The tight global supply and demand balance will further support prices,
and aluminum prices are expected to remain strong and volatile in 2026.

     POTENTIAL RISKS

     1.   Market Price Fluctuation Risk

          Escalating geopolitical conflicts and trade barriers, the impact of global economic uncertainty
          on the global market, and changes in domestic market supply and demand structure may
          lead to sharp fluctuations in prices of bulk raw materials and non-ferrous metals at home and
          abroad, potentially narrowing the Company’s product profit margin.


          P r e v e n t i o n a n d C o n t r o l M e a s u r e s: E s t a b l i s h a m u l t i-d i m e n s i o n a l p r e v e n t i o n a n d
          control system around market changes and competitive risks; adhere to the analysis of
          “macroeconomy + aluminum industry fundamentals” to timely avoid market risks; strengthen
          dynamic monitoring of key raw material market prices to maintain market sensitivity;
          reasonably control the pace of procurement, production and sales based on market conditions
          and the Company’s actual production and operation; conduct hedging in compliance to hedge
          against price fluctuation risks.


     2.   International Operation Risk

          The complex international environment and uncertainties in macroeconomy and geopolitics
          bring various potential impacts to international operations, which may adversely affect the
          supply of overseas bauxite resources of the Company.


          Prevention and Control Measures: Strengthen dynamic control over domestic self-mined ore
          production and strive to increase self-mined ore volume; intensify overseas ore shipment
          to ensure stable supply of ore resources; build a diversified imported ore resource security
          system, and consolidate the emergency reserve line for supply by vigorously expanding
          external markets; accelerate the development of new ore sources, focus on building overseas
          ore supply bases, and further improve resource security capacity.


     3.   Safety and Environmental Protection Risk

          With increasingly stringent national safety and environmental protection policies, the safety
          and environmental protection risks of the Company’s affiliated enterprises increase, and the
          growing number of new capacity and projects under construction raises safety risks.

5.   Exchange Rate Fluctuation Risk

     With the deepening of the Company’s international operations, large two-way fluctuations in
     the RMB exchange rate against the US dollar may adversely affect the Company’s operating
     performance and financial position.


     Prevention and Control Measures: Following the principle of “combination of futures and
     spot, natural hedging as the mainstay and derivative business as the supplement”, the
     Company conducts exchange rate hedging and standardized derivative business, handles
     foreign exchange settlement and sales reasonably based on foreign exchange trends, strictly
     controls exchange rate risks, and strives to minimize the adverse impact of exchange rate
     fluctuations to the greatest extent.

     DIVIDEND AND DIVIDEND POLICY

     Dividend policy

     1.   The basic principles of profit distribution are as follows:

          (1)   Taking full account of return to investors and distributing dividend to shareholders in
                proportion to the distributable dividend realised for the year, if the Company’s profit for
                the year and its cumulative undistributed profit are positive;


          (2)   Maintaining the continuity and stability of the Company’s dividend distribution policy,
                while at the same time taking care of the interest of the Company in the long term, the
                interest of the shareholders as a whole, as well as the sustainable development of the
                Company;


          (3)   The Company may distribute dividends in cash, in shares or in a combination of both
                cash and shares. The Company shall give priority to dividend distribution in cash.
                Subject to conditions, interim profit distribution may be made by the Company.




72   ALUMINUM CORPORATION OF CHINA LIMITED
                                                               Report of the Board (Continued)

2.    Procedures for considering the profit distribution plan:

      (1)   The Company’s profit distribution plan shall be prepared by the management and
            submitted to the Company’s Board for consideration. The Board shall thoroughly
            discuss the rationality of the profit distribution plan and form an ad hoc resolution
            before submitting to the general meeting for consideration.


      (2)   Where the Company has no cash dividend distribution proposal under the special
            circumstances, the Board shall explain the specific reasons for not distributing cash
            dividends, the exact purpose for the retained profit and the estimated investment
            return, submit the same to the general meeting for consideration after independent
            directors have expressed their opinions thereon, and disclose the same in the media
            designated by the Company.


3.    Implementation of the profit distribution plan:

      After the profit distribution plan has been resolved at the general meeting of the Company
      (or, if authorized by the general meeting, after the profit distribution plan has been resolved
      by the Board meeting of the Company), the Company shall complete the dividend distribution
      within two months after the date of the general meeting (Board meeting).

the distribution of the above interim dividend for 2025 on 17 October 2025.

EMPLOYEES AND PENSION SCHEMES
The Company had a standardised employment system, adheres to the basic principle of lawful
employment, strictly complied with the Labor Law of the People’s Republic of China and other
relevant laws and regulations, formulated and implemented internal management systems,
such as the Measures for the Administration of Labor Employment of Aluminum Corporation of
China Limited and the Management Measures for Open Recruitment of Employees of Aluminum
Corporation of China Limited, to strengthen and regulate the management of the Company’s
employment of labor and to earnestly safeguard the interests of its employees. The Company
adheres to the principle of equal employment opportunity, and resolutely prohibits discrimination
in recruitment, promotion, salary, or any other aspect based on ethnicity, race, gender, religious
beliefs, or any other factors.


As of 31 December 2025, the Group had 60,814 employees. The remuneration package of the
employees includes salaries, bonuses, allowances, subsidies and welfare benefits including medical
care, housing subsidies, maternity, unemployment, work-related injury, pension and other welfare
benefits.


The Company adhered to the principle of “equal pay for equal work” and the philosophy that
“contribution determines the remuneration”, established a more precise, flexible, standardised
and efficient income distribution system, explicitly the linkage between total wages and the
achievement of key performance indicators such as complete cost and total profit, implemented
differentiated incentives, and ensured that the total number of wages is tilted in favor of enterprises
with excellent costs, good benefits and high efficiency. On the principle of “as profitability rises,
wages rise, and as profitability decreases, wages decrease”, measures of “raising low wages
and expanding the group with middle wages” were taken to reasonably regulate the income gap
among employees. In terms of income distribution within the enterprise, the focus was tilted
towards science and technology, skills and other key employees in the production frontline and key
positions.




                                                                                   2025 ANNUAL REPORT     85
     Report of the Board (Continued)

     In order to achieve medium and long-term incentives, the Company implemented the Restricted
     Share Incentive Scheme, granting restricted shares to Directors, senior management, middle
     management and technical and business backbones of the Company, and formulated the
     corresponding implementation methods of the assessment and management measure, linking
     the Company’s performance, personal evaluation and incentive payment to further mobilize the
     management and business backbones of the Company and promote the long-term sustainable
     development of the Company. In 2024 and 2025, the unlocking conditions for the first unlocking
     period and the second unlocking period under the Restricted Share Incentive Scheme of the
     Company were satisfied, and a total of 94,658,198 restricted shares were unlocked for participants.
     Benefiting from the Company’s improved performance and sustained share price growth in recent
     years, employees have been able to share in the substantial gains arising from the Company’s value
     appreciation, thus effectively harnessing the motivational benefits.


     The Company strictly implemented the labor laws, regulations and policies promulgated by the State
     and local governments, and has established a retirement pension protection system covering all
     employees in accordance with the Social Insurance Law of the People’s Republic of China and the
     relevant requirements of local social insurance coordination, and all the full-time employees of the
     Group have participated in the basic pension insurance set by the government in accordance with
     the national policy. For the year ended 31 December 2025, the Group paid basic pension insurance
     premiums at 16% of the employees’ remuneration; at the same time, individual employees also
     contributed to basic pension insurance at a percentage of their own remuneration as set by the
     government. Upon employees reaching the statutory retirement age, the Company shall handle the
     retirement approval procedures, pension withdrawal procedures and social management procedures
     for the employees in accordance with the laws and regulations to ensure that the retired employees
     receive a monthly basic pension. In addition, in accordance with national policies and the relevant
     provisions of the Company’s system, the Company and eligible subsidiaries of the Company have
     established enterprise annuities plans. The expenses required for the enterprise annuities shall be
     paid jointly by the enterprises and the individual employees, with employees joined on a voluntary
     basis.


     As at 31 December 2025, the Group had no forfeited contributions available for deduction of
     contributions payable in future years. For the year ended 31 December 2025, the Group did not
     have a defined benefit plan at the level of the Group, but had a plan involving expenses related
     to some retired personnel of its subordinate units, which had an obligation to pay for their living
     expenses during their lifetime. The scope and amount of its impact are not significant to the Group.
     Please refer to Note 24 of the financial statements for details.

     MAJOR CUSTOMERS AND SUPPLIERS

     1.   Major customers

          The Group’s alumina is mainly sold to group companies engaged in primary aluminium and
          marketing and external customers. The Group’s primary aluminum is mainly sold to group
          companies engaged in marketing and external customers.


          The Company sells alumina products to customers mainly through long-term sales
          agreements and spot market sales. Long-term alumina sales contracts usually specify the
          annual or monthly sales volume of alumina, pricing mechanism, payment terms, place of
          delivery and method of delivery. When selling alumina through the spot market, the sales
          price is determined mainly after considering domestic and international supply and demand
          conditions.


          The Company sells primary aluminum products to customers mainly through three methods:
          (i) contract sales – the Company directly signs contracts with customers having long-term
          business relationships, with a contract validity period of usually one year; (ii) sales through
          futures contracts on the Shanghai Futures Exchange; (iii) spot market sales.


          The Company is committed to continuously optimizing product quality management and
          customer service measures to systematically improve product quality and customer
          satisfaction. By strengthening the construction of quality management system, deepening
          the “interactive grid” quality management model, and carrying out quality management
          certification, the Company strives to build a new industry benchmark for quality. While
          strengthening quality management, the Company continuously improves customer service
          quality, optimizes the customer experience throughout the life cycle by improving internal
          management systems to standardize product sales service processes and clarify transaction
          dispute resolution methods, and maintains stable customer relationships by timely
          communicating with customers and properly resolving customer complaints through analysis.


          In 2025, the sales to the top five customers of the Company amounted to RMB49,414.81
          million and accounted for 20.49% of the Company’s total annual sales, among which, sales
          to related parties were RMB29,869.11 million, accounting for 12.39% of the Company’s total
          annual sales.




88   ALUMINUM CORPORATION OF CHINA LIMITED
                                                              Report of the Board (Continued)

2.   Suppliers

     The Company has built a streamlined, clean and low-cost supply chain system by establishing
     a sound whole-process supplier management mechanism, strengthening supply chain
     management in multiple dimensions, improving risk prevention and control, and promoting
     supplier capability enhancement. Strictly abiding by relevant national laws and regulations,
     the Company has established a supplier life cycle management system specifying supplier
     access, assessment, evaluation and withdrawal. The Company continued to optimize
     the “Green Star Chain 2.0” procurement system, realizing a full-chain online closed-
     loop management from planning, sourcing, execution to settlement, covering all levels of
     enterprises and integrating resources from more than 100 suppliers. The system significantly
     improved procurement efficiency and transparency through “one-time entry, automatic flow”,
     laying a digital foundation for cost savings and enhanced market competitiveness. Meanwhile,
     through diversified exchange and training activities, the Company empowered supplier
     capability building, strengthened their sustainable development practices, and deepened
     strategic cooperative relationships.


     The Company deeply integrates the concept of sustainable development into the supply
     chain management system, and has established a supplier ESG governance mechanism
     supervised by the Board of Directors and ESG Committee and implemented on a regular basis
     by the Marketing Management Department. In the supplier access process, the Company
     incorporates ISO quality management, environmental management, occupational health and
     safety system certifications into the scoring model, and gives priority to suppliers with ESG
     certifications. The system explicitly prohibits corruption, false advertising, infringement of
     trade secrets and other acts in the supply chain, and systematically verifies suppliers’ illegal
     operation and business ethics records in access assessment, imposing a ban on suppliers
     with serious adverse records. To enhance supply chain resilience and stability, the Company
     continuously improves the risk management system, integrates risk management and
     control requirements into key links such as procurement, trade and logistics, and achieves
     full-process risk prevention and control through annual supplier risk assessment, on-site
     inspections of key suppliers, strengthened daily supervision and inspection, and realized full
     process risk prevention and control.


     In 2025, the procurement from the top five suppliers of the Company amounted to
     RMB40,991.21 million, accounting for 20.53% of the total annual procurement, among which,
     procurement from related parties was RMB10,641.91 million, accounting for 5.33% of the
     Company’s total annual procurement.

     Report on Corporate Governance and Internal Control (Continued)

     During the Reporting Period, there was a brief deviation by the Company from code provision C.2.1
     of the CG Code, details of which are as follows:


     Pursuant to code provision C.2.1 of the CG Code, the roles of chairman and chief executive shall
     be separate and shall not be performed by the same individual. In accordance with the Company’s
     announcement dated 24 February 2025, Mr. Shi Zhirong resigned as the chairman and an Executive
     Director of the Company and from all the positions in each of the special committees under the
     Board on 24 February 2025 due to work arrangements. In view of the resignation of Mr. Shi
     Zhirong, in order to ensure the normal operation of the Company and the Board, in accordance
     with the provisions of the Company Law and the Articles of Association, and as considered and
     approved at the thirty-first meeting of the eighth session of the Board of the Company convened
     on 28 February 2025 and the first meeting of the ninth session of the Board convened on 26 June
     2025, all Directors of the Company jointly recommend Mr. He Wenjian, being the Executive Director
     and general manager, to act as the chairman and legal representative of the Company until a new
     chairman is elected by the Board of the Company. Therefore, the Company has a brief deviation
     from code provision C.2.1 of the CG Code during the Reporting Period. Nevertheless, given that the
     Board is composed of experienced and distinguished individuals and that the Board has a sufficient
     number of Independent Non-executive Directors, the Board believes that through the operation of
     the Board, it is sufficient to ensure the balanced distribution of power and authority. Therefore, Mr.
     He Wenjian concurrently acting as chairman and serving as general manager of the Company does
     not impair the balanced distribution of power and authority between the Board and management of
     the Company. In this case, deviating from code provision C.2.1 of the CG Code is still appropriate.
     Mr. He Wenjian resigned as the general manager of the Company on 6 November 2025. On the
     same day, at the sixth meeting of the ninth session of the Board of the Company, Mr. He Wenjian
     was elected as the chairman of the ninth session of the Board of the Company, and the Board
     agreed to appoint Mr. Zhang Ruizhong as the general manager of the Company. Therefore, the
     Company is currently in compliance with the requirements of code provision C.2.1 of the CG Code.

external auditors, asset valuers and independent financial advisers to provide professional and
independent opinions to the Board in accordance with the provisions of the Articles of Association
and the Rules of Procedures for the Board Meetings when considering matters such as periodic
reports, significant related party transactions and material asset reorganisation. All Directors of the
Company may seek advice from the Company Secretary, internal legal team or personnel of any
functional department, or request to engage external professional bodies to provide independent
advice and the expenses incurred shall be borne by the Company.


The Company will further refine the working policy for independent Directors according to the
Measures for the Administration of Independent Directors of Listed Companies and the Detailed
Implementation Rules for Independent Directors, so as to improve the duty performance capability
of independent Directors, and give full play to the role of independent Directors in corporate
governance.


The Company has reviewed the implementation and effectiveness of the aforesaid mechanisms
and considers that the aforesaid mechanisms are able to ensure that the Board is provided with
independent views and opinions.

      The Company has adopted the Board Diversity Policy, and considered the diversity of the members
      of the Board from various aspects (including but not limited to gender, age, region, professional
      competence, educational background and experience) based on the Company’s business model
      and specific needs. After reviewing the implementation of the Board Diversity Policy in 2025, the
      Company considers that it has been effectively implemented. In terms of the implementation of the
      Board Diversity Policy, the Company has adopted the following measurable objectives:


      •    There is at least one female member on the Board;


      •    There is at least one Independent Non-executive Director on the Board who resides in Hong
           Kong;


      •    There is at least one financial expert on the Board who possess professional qualifications
           and experience in finance and audit recognized by the regulatory authorities;


      •    Non-executive Directors (including Independent Non-executive Directors) account for more
           than one-half of the members of the Board, and Independent Non-executive Directors account
           for one-third of the members of the Board;


      •    The age composition of Directors is reasonable, with one aged between 40-50, five aged
           between 50-60, and two aged over 60;


      •    The professional backgrounds of the Directors are diverse. Each Director of the Company has
           different academic qualifications and professional backgrounds, and has deep attainments and
           rich experience in metal mining, production technology, corporate management, law, financial
           accounting, finance and capital operation.


      As of 31 December 2025, the Company has achieved the measurable objectives set out in the
      Board Diversity Policy.

The major duties of the Board of the Company include: deciding on the Company’s operating
plans and investment proposals, formulating the Company’s profit distribution and loss recovery
proposals; formulating the Company’s debt and financial policies, and the issuance of bonds
and other debt instruments; determining plans for material acquisitions or disposals as well as
mergers, demergers and dissolution of the Company; determining the establishment of internal
management departments of the Company; appointment and termination of senior management;
formulating the basic management system of the Company; promoting the establishment of a
compliance management system and monitoring the performance of compliance management of
managers; developing the ESG management strategies and monitoring the ESG governance efforts
of the management; formulating the share incentive scheme; deciding on the Company’s external
investment, purchase or sale of assets, equity and other capital operation plans within the scope
of the authorization of general meeting, and convening general meetings and implementing the
resolutions of general meetings, etc. Details of the functions of the Board are set out in the Articles

Limited” under “Circulars and Announcements” on the page of “Investor Relations” on the website

The Company generally formulates the plans for the Board and general meetings and major topics
of the meetings for the following year at the end of the previous year, and sends the meeting plans
to all Directors to facilitate their schedule and ensure that each Director has the opportunity to raise
matters for discussion and being included in the agenda of the Board meetings; for the matters
which are required temporarily for consideration by the Board or the change of meeting time, the
Company also communicates with and reports to the Directors in advance and agrees on the time
and manner of holding the meetings so that each Director may attend all meetings as much as
possible.


Before the Board meeting, the Company, in accordance within the time stipulated in the Articles
of Association and the Rules of Procedures for the Board Meetings, always sends the meeting
documents and relevant materials to the Directors for their review in advance, consults Directors’
opinions on the matters concerned in the resolutions, and answers the Directors’ concerns or
makes thematic reports. In particular, the Company provides detailed explanations on matters such
as profit distribution proposal, provision for impairment of assets and related party transactions, and
arranges for intermediaries such as auditors and independent financial advisers to explain or provide
opinions on periodic reports and significant related party transactions, so as to provide the Directors
with a basis for decision-making.

CHAIRMAN AND GENERAL MANAGER

As the legal representative of the Company, the chairman presides over the Board, aiming to ensure
that the Board is acting in the best interests of the Company, operates effectively, duly performs
its responsibilities and engages in discussions on significant and appropriate matters, as well as
Directors’ access to accurate, timely and clear information. On the other hand, the general manager
heads the management and is responsible for the daily operation of the Company, including
implementation of policies adopted by the Board and reporting to the Board in respect of the overall
operation of the Company.


Pursuant to code provision C.2.1 of the CG Code, the roles of chairman and chief executive shall be
separate and shall not be performed by the same individual. As of the date of this annual report, Mr.
He Wenjian is the chairman of the Board of the Company, and Mr. Zhang Ruizhong is the general
manager of the Company.


During the Reporting Period, Mr Shi Zhirong, the former chairman of the Company, resigned on
24 February 2025, and as considered and approved by the 31st meeting of the eighth session of
the Board held on 28 February 2025 and 1st meeting of the ninth session of the Board held on
26 June 2025 by the Company, in order to ensure the normal operation of the Company and its
Board, and in accordance with the provisions of the Company Law and the Articles of Association,
all Directors of the Company jointly recommend Mr. He Wenjian, being the Executive Director and
general manager, to act as the chairman and legal representative of the Company until the Board

      of the Company elects the new chairman. Mr. He Wenjian resigned as the general manager of

AUDIT COMMITTEE

The Audit Committee has been established under the Board of the Company, the duties of which
mainly include reviewing the financial reports, internal and external audits, internal control, risk
management, corporate governance of the Company, considering the appointment of independent
auditors and approving audit and audit-related services, and supervising the Company’s internal
financial reporting procedures and management policies. Furthermore, following the abolition of the
Supervisory Committee, the Audit Committee has assumed the supervisory functions previously
exercised by the Supervisory Committee, including overseeing the Company’s production
and operational activities, and monitoring the performance of duties by Directors and senior
management.


Pursuant to Rule 3.21 of the Hong Kong Listing Rules, the Audit Committee of the Board of the
Company consists of three Independent Non-executive Directors, including a financial expert.


During the Reporting Period, the Audit Committee of the eighth session of the Board of the

      The Company has established work procedures for the Audit Committee for the performance of

      report of the Company after the external auditors issued their preliminary audit opinions and passed

      internal control systems have been established, which included considering whether the Company

      auditing and financial reporting duties, and whether relevant staff were well trained and the relevant
      budget was sufficient. The Audit Committee is of the view that the Company had complied with the
      requirements of the above corporate risk management and internal control systems during 2025.

EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING

According to the Articles of Association of the Company, a single shareholder or any two or more
shareholders together holding more than 10% (inclusive) of the Company’s issued share capital is
(are) entitled to request an extraordinary general meeting or class meeting to be convened. Such
requests must specify the topics of the meeting in writing and must be submitted to the convener,
the contact information of whom is set out in the section entitled “Enquiry to the Board” in this
chapter. Shareholders shall follow the Rules of Procedures for the Shareholders’ Meetings of
Aluminum Corporation of China Limited set out in the “Circulars and Announcements” under the
section of “Investor Relations” on the website of the Company.


PROPOSALS AT THE GENERAL MEETING

According to the Articles of Association of the Company, shareholders who alone or together hold
more than 1% of the Company’s issued share capital is (are) entitled to submit additional proposals
to the convener by written request at least ten working days prior to the general meeting of the
Company. The contact information of the convener is set out in the section entitled “Enquiry to the
Board” in this chapter. Shareholders shall follow the Rules of Procedures for the General Meeting
of Aluminum Corporation of China Limited set out in the “Circulars and Announcements” under the
section of “Investor Relations” on the website of the Company.

INFORMATION DISCLOSURE

Upholding a high degree of responsibility towards investors, the Company consistently regards
information disclosure as a core responsibility in safeguarding market fairness and protecting
investor rights. By establishing a comprehensive, multi-tiered information disclosure management
system, the Company rigorously fulfils its disclosure obligations to ensure investors receive timely,
accurate and fair access to information, thereby minimising investment risks of investors to the
greatest extent possible.


To standardise the management of information disclosure, the Company has formulated and
amended from time to time the Management Measures of Information Disclosure of Aluminum
Corporation of China Limited (《中國鋁業股份有限公司信息披露管理辦法》) and the Management
Measures of Inside Information and Insiders of Aluminum Corporation of China Limited (《中國鋁
業股份有限公司內幕信息及知情人管理辦法》), which stipulates stringent requirements concerning
the regulatory authority, personnel and their responsibilities of information disclosure, principles of
information disclosure to be followed, disclosure documents and content, approval procedures for

RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROL
The goal of the Company’s risk management and internal control is to reasonably ensure the legality
and compliance of our business management, asset security, authenticity and completeness of
financial reports and related information, improve operational efficiency and effectiveness, and
promote the realization of development strategies. However, due to the inherent limitations of
internal control, it may only provide reasonable assurance for achieving the aforementioned goals.
In addition, due to changes in circumstances that may lead to inappropriate internal controls or a
decline in compliance with control policies and procedures, there is a certain risk in inferring the
effectiveness of future internal controls based on internal control evaluation results. The Company’s
risk management and internal control system aims to manage rather than eliminate the risk of
failure to achieve business objectives, and may only provide reasonable rather than absolute
guarantees that there will be no significant misstatements or losses.

Establishing and effectively implementing risk management and internal controls is the responsibility
of the Board of the Company. As a special committee established under the Board, the Audit
Committee of the Company has supervised and inspected the establishment, comprehensiveness
and implementation of the risk management and internal control system of the Company, and
regularly discussed with the management on the implementation of the risk management and
internal control in order to ensure that the Company has established an effective risk management
and internal control system. The management is responsible for arrangement and leadership of
the daily operation of the risk management and internal control of the Company; the Company’s
management innovation department (reform office, digital management department) functions
as the department responsible for risk management, the finance department (capital operations
department) serves as the department responsible for internal control, and the audit department
acts as the department responsible for independent internal control evaluations, carrying out the
specific work accordingly.


                                                                                  2025 ANNUAL REPORT    129
      Report on Corporate Governance and Internal Control (Continued)

      The Company organises the management of the Company, the supervisory departments of the
      headquarters, business departments and subsidiaries to accurately identify major risks of the year
      based on the latest changes in the external environment and their own business development at
      the beginning of each year, and analyses each major risk, formulates countermeasures, prepares
      a comprehensive risk management report and submits it to the Board of the Company for
      consideration and approval after the report is considered by the Audit Committee of the Board.
      The Company dynamically monitors major risks, tracks the implementation and effectiveness of
      preventive and control measures, regularly reports to the management the regulating status and
      changing trend of such risks, and puts forward management suggestions in a timely manner.


      In 2025, the Company further optimised and refined its internal control system, promoting the
      establishment of audit and risk committees within its subsidiaries, with the internal control
      assessment of “full coverage within three years” programme successfully concluded, and the
      Company organised all levels of enterprises to conduct 2024 annual and 2025 interim internal
      control self-assessment, promptly rectifying identified minor deficiencies with no material or
      significant defects detected.


      The Audit Committee of the Board of the Company conducts regular reviews over the risk
      management and internal control of the Company on an annual basis, receives reports from relevant
      functional departments, discusses key issues with management and functional units, examines the
      Company’s comprehensive risk management, internal control evaluation, and internal control audit
      supervision, and submits relevant reports to the Board for consideration and reports the work to the
      Board.

           (2) Restricted Share Incentive Scheme

                 At the 24th meeting of the seventh session of the Board and the 12th meeting of the
                 seventh session of the Supervisory Committee of the Company held on 21 December
                 2021, the Company reviewed and approved the relevant resolutions on the Company’s
                 Restricted Share Incentive Scheme (Draft) in 2021 and its summary, and agreed to
                 the implementation of the 2021 Restricted Share Incentive Scheme to grant not more
                 than 141,000,000 A shares (representing approximately 0.82% of the Company’s
                 17,155,632,078 shares in issue at the end of the Reporting Period) to not more than
                 1,192 Participants. The Restricted Share Incentive Scheme is valid from the date of
                 completion of registration of the first grant of restricted shares to the date of unlocking
                 of all restricted shares granted to the Participants or the date of repurchase, subject to a
                 maximum period of 72 months. The purpose of the Restricted Share Incentive Scheme
                 is to further improve the corporate governance structure, establish a sound sustainable
                 and stable incentive restraint mechanism, bring sustainable returns to shareholders,
                 build a bond of interests among shareholders, the Company and employees, fully
                 mobilize the enthusiasm of core employees, support the strategic realization and long-
                 term steady development of the Company, attract, retain and motivate outstanding
                 talents and advocate the concept of sustainable development of the Company and
                 its employees together. The Participants of the Incentive Scheme include directors,
                 senior management, middle management and core technical (business) backbone of
                 the Company. The number of Restricted Shares granted to any one Participant shall
                 not exceed 1% of the total share capital of the Company prior to the submission of
                 the Restricted Share Incentive Scheme to the general meeting for consideration. The
                 date of determining the price of the Restricted Shares under the first grant is the date
                 of announcement of the draft Restricted Share Incentive Scheme. The price of grant
                 shall not be less than the par value of the shares (RMB1.00) and shall not be less than
                 the higher of: (1) 50% of the average trading price of the Company’s A shares for the 1
                 trading day prior to the announcement of the Restricted Share Incentive Scheme, being
                 RMB3.08 per share; (2) 50% of the average trading price of the Company’s A shares
                 for the 20 trading days prior to the announcement of the Restricted Share Incentive
                 Scheme, being RMB2.98 per share. The price of grant of reserved restricted shares
                 shall not be less than the par value of the shares (RMB1.00) and not less than 50%
                 of the higher of the following prices: (1) The average trading price of the Company’s
                 A shares for 1 trading day prior to the announcement of the resolution of the Board
                 to grant reserved restricted shares; (2) one of the average trading prices of the
                 Company’s A shares for 20 trading days, 60 trading days or 120 trading days prior to the
                 announcement of the Board resolution to grant reserved restricted shares.
